note: Real projects shown on the Threadlands map. Added by the Threadlands team or by visitors, after review. Each has a public source.

projects.name: Parque Ecológico Lago de Texcoco
projects.summary: About 14,000 hectares of restored lake, wetland and parkland on the former site of the cancelled airport, east of the city. Opened in September 2024.

source.title: El Imparcial: AMLO inaugura el Parque Ecológico Lago de Texcoco (2 Sep 2024)

projects.area: Old Lake Texcoco, State of Mexico

next.text: Visit free, Tuesday to Sunday, 7:00 to 19:00. CONANP runs free birdwatching and environmental education workshops, and winter is when migratory birds fill the lagoons.

source.title: Chilango: Parque Ecológico Lago de Texcoco actividades gratis 2026 (29 Dec 2025)

projects.name: Parque Lineal Gran Canal
projects.summary: A linear park on the bed of the old Gran Canal drain in Venustiano Carranza: 708 new trees and 24 wells that return rainwater to the aquifer. First stage about 840 m, opened 2021.

source.title: Mexico City tourism: Parque Lineal Gran Canal

next.text: No open call or event found right now. It is a public park, open to walk. Follow for updates.

projects.name: Jardín Flotante Tlallipan
projects.summary: A 1.8 km elevated garden and walking route over Calzada de Tlalpan, between Pino Suárez and Chabacano: 176 trees, thousands of shrubs and more than 80,000 pollinator plants. Opened June 2026.
projects.area: Calzada de Tlalpan, between Pino Suárez and Chabacano

next.text: Drop in: free culture workshops (painting, papier-mâché), a pollinator garden, and low-cost fruit and vegetables from local producers.

source.title: Crónica: Jardín Flotante Tlallipan reaches half a million visitors (29 Aug 2026)

projects.name: Cosecha de Lluvia (rain harvesting at home)
projects.summary: Free rooftop rainwater systems for homes with poor water service, started in Iztapalapa and Xochimilco: 73,021 systems installed since 2019, about 1.7 billion liters harvested (August 2024).

source.title: Mexico Business News: SEDEMA installs 73,000 rain harvesting systems (26 Aug 2024)

projects.area: Started in Iztapalapa and Xochimilco; now in rounds by borough

next.text: Sign-up opens in rounds by area. The last round we could confirm was for parts of Coyoacán and Tlalpan (July 2025). No open call confirmed for 2026 yet: follow for updates.

source.title: Yahoo Noticias: Abren preregistro para Cosecha de Lluvia y Calentadores Solares (22 Jul 2025)

projects.name: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park
projects.summary: A 4.5 ha park in central Bangkok built to hold rainwater: a tilted lawn, retention ponds and a constructed wetland catch storm runoff, holding about a million gallons, so the surrounding streets flood less.

projects.name: Parc résilient Pierre-Bédard (sponge park)
projects.who: Ville de Montréal, borough of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve
projects.summary: Montreal's largest sponge park: it can hold about 5,700 cubic meters of rainwater during heavy storms, with bioswales on the surrounding streets. Opened August 2025; over $15 million. Map pin approximate.

source.title: Ville de Montréal: Pierre-Bédard becomes the city's largest sponge park (30 Aug 2025)

projects.name: India Basin Waterfront Park
projects.summary: A 10-acre waterfront park in Bayview–Hunters Point joining India Basin Shoreline Park with 900 Innes: restored shoreline habitat, a gravel beach, a pier and a boathouse. Final phase broke ground August 2025, due late 2027 or early 2028.

source.title: SF.gov: Mayor Lurie breaks ground on final phase of India Basin Waterfront Park (19 Aug 2025)

projects.name: ForestaMi: 3 million trees for greater Milan
projects.who: Comune di Milano, Città Metropolitana, Regione Lombardia, Parco Nord, Parco Agricolo Sud and partners; research by Politecnico di Milano
projects.summary: Planting across the metropolitan area since 2019, with a goal of 3 million trees and shrubs: about 640,000 planted by October 2026. Covers the whole metro area; map pin at Parco Nord.

source.title: Euronews: Milan, from one of Europe's most polluted cities to a model for nature restoration (29 Oct 2026)

projects.name: TALEA: green cells against urban heat
projects.who: Comune di Bologna with Università di Bologna and partners; EU Urban Initiative
projects.summary: A network of compact green climate refuges in public spaces to cool heat islands, with three pilot areas between the Fossolo district and the historic center. Over €6.2 million, running December 2024 to May 2028. Map pin approximate.

source.title: Quotidiano.net: TALEA, Bologna's green cells against heat islands (Feb 2026)

ideas.greening-for-heat: Trees and green space against heat
